_comment: THE AUTHORED LAYER, AND THE ONLY ONE. Every visual choice in the renderer lives here: which labeling
drives which channel, and what values that channel takes. This file contains no node data, no edge
data and no positions. It references labelings by id from the fixed set and nothing else.
Palettes are declared once per labeling rather than per viewpoint, so a labeling gets the same visual
treatment wherever it appears. That is cross view consistency by construction rather than by care.
If a viewpoint wants something no labeling carries, that is a missing labeling. Derive it; do not
write data here.
A viewpoint names the frozen layout it uses. The authored choice is WHICH frozen layout, never the
positions themselves: no coordinate appears in this file, and the renderer computes none.
A scalar bound to colour needs a scale rather than a palette. Its domain is taken from the range the
labeling itself declares, never from node values read off the data.
Six distinct HUES, not shades of one. The first attempt grouped the four vocabulary kinds as four
blues to signal that they belong together, and that failed: the closest pair sat at a perceptual
distance of 17, below the threshold of 20 that every other palette here clears, so abbrev and
inductive were not tellable apart on the canvas. Grouping by hue family and distinguishing values
are the same channel and cannot both be had; distinguishing wins, and the grouping is carried by
the legend and by the two weight labelings instead.
Theorem takes the lightest and least saturated colour on purpose, because it is 68 percent of the
nodes and a saturated majority drowns the rest. Axiom takes the loudest, being four nodes that
would otherwise vanish. The six categories come from the environment; only the colours are chosen.
One scale per weight labeling, all of the same shape, because size is compared WITHIN a mode and
never across modes. Each scale takes its domain from the range its own labeling declares, so two
modes with different maxima both fill the same radius band and a switch never rescales the frame.
That is deliberate: theorem weight and vocabulary weight are not commensurable, so a shared
absolute scale would invite exactly the comparison the split exists to prevent.
The size channel is a CHOICE, offered here and switchable in the renderer. A viewpoint still
declares which mode drives size by default; selecting another overrides that one channel and
nothing else. Positions are frozen in the layout and no mode touches them.
Five modes along two independent decompositions of the same total: statement against proof splits
the ROUTES a dependency travelled, theorem against vocabulary splits the DESTINATIONS it reached.
The two are not variants of each other and are listed in that order.
